Key.English: SAFE / CARELESS groups switch to AWARE while suspicious, and back when calm.
Groups that identify you switch to COMBAT.
The soldier who first notices your vehicle glances at it (they turn their head, so they see more).
Once suspicious, the best placed soldier keeps looking at your vehicle until the group calms down.
Every soldier of a suspicious group turns to watch the vehicle (stronger than looking).
How close to a soldier your weapon must point to count as aiming at them (half-angle).
Suspicion speed while your weapon or turret points at a soldier. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
When a pursuit is given up (you were too fast or too far), the pursuers alert the area too.
Groups and outposts within this distance of the pursuers hear their alerts.
Groups hearing an alert start SEARCHING with at least this suspicion.
Suspicion speed in a vehicle of a side allied to the watching AI. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
Helicopters and planes can disguise the people inside.\nOff = aircraft never give cover.
Boats can disguise the people inside.\nOff = boats never give cover.
Civilian cars, trucks, boats and aircraft disguise the people inside.\nOff = civilian vehicles do not hide anyone.
Vehicles of the watching AI's own or allied side disguise the people inside.\nExample: BLUFOR players in a captured OPFOR truck fool OPFOR.

Vehicles of a side the watching AI is at war with can still disguise the people inside,\nbut suspicion builds much faster (see 'Vehicle Faction').\nExample: BLUFOR players in an unarmed BLUFOR Hunter at an OPFOR checkpoint.
Your own side's vehicles are recognised and attacked on sight.
Trucks and unarmed cars can bluff their way through, gun trucks, APCs and tanks cannot.
Even armed vehicles, tanks and APCs start undercover (not recommended for assaults).
Server permission for the watched / identified hints and the ACE status readout.\nOff = players get no hints about how suspicious the AI are.
Aircraft above this height get proportionally less attention.\nExample: 60 = at 120 m suspicion builds half as fast.
When a group sees you again in another vehicle or kit, it keeps this share of its suspicion.\n1 = changing makes no difference. 0 = a complete fresh start.
Alerted SAFE / CARELESS groups switch to AWARE.
Seats that only see out through optics or periscopes (e.g. a BTR driver) count as armored\neven when the vehicle is not in the class list.
Comma-separated vehicle classes treated as armored (child classes included).\nExample: Tank,Wheeled_APC_F
Scales 'Face-to-face minimum visibility' for armored seats (a guard at the hull still cannot see in well).
In tanks, APCs and IFVs with closed hatches the AI cannot see who is inside. They can only judge\nthe vehicle, so suspicion builds much slower. Turned out or firing from a port = normal rules.
Armored: only behaviour gives it away

On = a closed armored vehicle driven calmly builds no suspicion at all (nobody can see in) and old suspicion fades.
It only builds while it gives itself away: speeding or off-road near them, lights off at night, honking,
pointing a gun at them, visible damage or parking next to them for long. Ramming always identifies.
Off = it builds slowly from the vehicle alone (Armored hull visibility).

How much of the vehicle's visibility counts while the crew sits behind armor.\nLower = armored vehicles are harder to see through. 1 = no protection.\nExample: 0.25 = a BMP that gives itself away builds suspicion about a quarter as fast as a car.
Suspicion speed for alert soldiers. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
Suspicion speed for soldiers in combat. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.\nLower = they are busy with the fight and pay less attention to traffic.
Suspicion speed for relaxed soldiers. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.\nExample: 0.7 = bored sentries are slower to notice.
Suspicion speed for soldiers in stealth mode. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.\nHigher = they are watching carefully.

Suspicion gained per second when an alert soldier gets a clear look at you up close.\nHigher = identified faster. Lower = more time to pass through.\nExample: 12 = about 8 s of a clear close look from 0 to 100%.
Groups near the reported position start SEARCHING.
Receiving groups recognise the vehicle on sight and attack its covered occupants.
Chance per identifying group that a bulletin is sent.
Shortest time to send. Killing or knocking out the radioman first cancels it.
On identification a radioman may broadcast you and your vehicle over a long range.
Groups that identified you because of gunfire or attacks also roll.
Groups farther from the sender do not hear it. 0 = the whole side.
The receiving side builds suspicion faster against you in any vehicle.
How long a reported vehicle stays known.
Distance from the identification within which that side recognises the vehicle. 0 = everywhere.
The vehicle someone was identified in is recognised on sight by that side nearby (see range).
If a mission or another undercover script makes a unit captive, RADS ignores it.\nKeep on when combining RADS with other undercover scripts.
Suspicion speed in a civilian vehicle. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
A group you fought within this many seconds keeps fighting you after you get in.
Identifying one person in a vehicle identifies everyone undercover in it.
The convoy multiplier never goes above this.
Extra suspicion per vehicle in view
Each additional convoy vehicle the group can see adds this to the suspicion speed.\nExample: 0.15 = three vehicles in view build 1.3x as fast.
Undercover vehicles driving close together in the same direction count as one convoy.
Vehicles must stay together this long before they count as a convoy (two cars meeting at a junction do not).
Vehicles within this distance of each other (chains count) form a convoy.
What happens to the other vehicles of a convoy when one of them is identified (by that group).
Every vehicle is judged on its own.
They get the spill-over suspicion and are SEARCHED for.
The whole convoy is identified at once.
Suspicion the other convoy vehicles get when 'Become suspects' is chosen.
AI soldiers of a covered side riding with an undercover player are undercover too.\nOff = enemy AI shoot at the vehicle because of the AI passenger.
OPFOR players can hide their identity inside vehicles.\nTurn on when OPFOR is the player side.
Technical: other machines wait this long after you get in before judging you, so the entry snapshot is used.\nLeave at 2 unless told otherwise.
Independent players can hide their identity inside vehicles.\nTurn on when INDFOR is the player side.
BLUFOR players (and their AI passengers) can hide their identity inside vehicles.\nOff = BLUFOR is always detected normally.
When a covered unit (or its vehicle) hurts an AI soldier, that soldier's group reacts.
How far above 'Suspicious at' heavy damage pushes suspicion straight away.\n0 = only to the suspicious level. 100% = up to just below identification for a wreck.
Visibly damaged vehicles (broken glass, bullet holes, burning) build suspicion faster:\nmultiplier = 1 + visible damage x this. 0 = damage does not matter.
On = a group hurt by someone it did not see only starts SEARCHING.\nOff = it identifies the attacker anyway.
Suspicion given to a group hurt by an attacker it did not see.
A vehicle with at least this much visible damage makes the group SUSPICIOUS the moment they see it.\n100% = off.
What is logged besides events and identification reports.
An evaluation that adds a lot of suspicion is logged on its own.
Evaluations kept per group and unit and printed with every report.
With 'Also big jumps', an evaluation adding at least this much is logged.

Writes every RADS decision to the RPT of the machine that owns the AI (server / headless client) and of the player:\nidentifications with full history, state changes, ramming, hits, shots, shares, syncs, truces, pursuits, cover changes.
Draws every nearby group's suspicion of you over its closest member (needs 'Publish suspicion live'). Per player.
Group owners broadcast suspicion every evaluation so overlays and Zeus Inspect stay live. Costs network traffic.
Suspicion lost per second while nobody in the group can see you.\nHigher = they forget you fast. Lower = they stay wary longer.\nExample: 1.5 = from 60% back to 0% in 40 s out of sight.

How quickly seeing you gets harder beyond the close look range: (close range / distance) ^ this.\nHigher = distance protects you more.\nExample: 1.5 with 40 m: 35% as effective at 80 m, 9% at 200 m, 3% at 400 m.
Master switch for the whole undercover system.\nOff = every player is back to normal Arma detection right away (AI shoot on sight).
Suspicion speed while the group is fighting another enemy. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
Getting out in view reveals at (%)
Getting out of the vehicle in view of a group at or above this suspicion reveals you to it.
Suspicion speed above the fast drive-by speed. 1 = no protection. 0.4 = 40% speed.
Above this speed the AI only get a short glimpse of you.\nExample: 50 = passing at 60 km/h is much safer than crawling past.
Firing a weapon from cover gets you identified by nearby groups and by groups that see you.
Any group with line of sight to the shooter (within spotting range) identifies them.
Groups within this distance of an unsuppressed shot identify the shooter.
Fleeing a stop gets you identified on the spot. Should they also radio a bulletin?
The vehicle you fled in is recognised on sight within the bulletin range.
Driving more than this far from where you stopped, during the inspection, counts as fleeing.
Driving faster than this during the inspection counts as fleeing.
How much fog hides you. 0 = fog does nothing. 1 = thick fog hides you completely.
A pursuing vehicle signals you to stop once it is this close.
Groups start a pursuit once their suspicion reaches the follow threshold (searching groups always may).
Suspicion at which a group starts following or chasing you instead of just watching.
A foot patrol gives up once the vehicle is this far away (they cannot catch a car).
A group that identified you forgets you after not seeing you this long, and your disguise works again.
Width of the cone a soldier is really looking at. Outside it only peripheral vision applies.\nExample: 140 = roughly what a person takes in without turning their head.
Suspicion speed in a vehicle of the same side but another faction. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
General look = civilian clothes, military uniform, helmets... Matching = item by item against\nwhat the watching side itself wears (see 'Gear Reference').
Old behaviour: side of the uniform, armored helmet/vest, NVG, visible weapon.
Each visible item is compared with the enemy's own kit.
General look always. Item matching only when you wear their (or an allied) uniform: it tells a good disguise from a sloppy one. Enemy fatigues are not punished twice (recommended).
Strict: both multipliers always apply, enemy fatigues count twice.
Uniform, vest, helmet, goggles, backpack and visible weapons change how fast suspicion builds.\nOff = gear is ignored.
Item matching never raises suspicion speed above this.
Item matching never lowers suspicion speed below this.
Suspicion speed for each visible item that is exactly what they wear. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
Suspicion speed for each visible item that none of them wears. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.\nExample: 1.15 with three wrong items = about 1.5x.
Suspicion speed for each empty slot they always fill (no helmet when every guard wears one). 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
Comma-separated item classes that never count, good or bad (mission-specific kit).\nExample: H_Cap_red,G_Aviator
Collect enemy gear at mission start
10 s after the mission starts, every side without a Gear Reference list gets one built from what its AI wear.\nOff = use the group's own kit until a list is set.
What the AI compare your kit against when 'How gear is judged' uses matching.
What the soldiers of the watching group wear right now.
Only the lists set by the Gear Reference module or API.
The list when one exists, otherwise the group, otherwise every unit of that side (recommended).
Suspicion speed for each item of the same model but another variant (other camo). 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
How much each slot counts (slot:weight, comma-separated). 2 = counts double, 0 = ignored.\nSlots: uniform, vest, headgear, primary, launcher, backpack, facewear.
Gear counts fully within this distance and fades out by twice this distance.\nExample: 50 = nobody can read your uniform at 100 m.
Wearing a military uniform of a covered side (e.g. BLUFOR fatigues).
Carrying a rifle or launcher in a seat that shows it (turned out, firing seat, open vehicle).
Units wearing the gear ticked below get no cover in vehicles at all (normal detection).\nOn foot always uses normal detection anyway.

Performance budget: how many enemy groups are checked in a single frame.\nLower = smoother frame rate with many AI. Higher = every group is updated sooner.\nLeave at 6 unless you have hundreds of AI groups.
After firing you cannot regain cover for this long. 0 = off.\nExample: 120 = jumping into another car right after a firefight does not work for 2 minutes.
Suspicion speed wearing an armored helmet. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
Off = only reversing up and parking rear-on are caught.\nOn = also a slow vehicle close by whose crew is hidden any other way (tinted or blocked windows).
How much of the vehicle's visibility counts when the crew cannot be seen at all.\n0 = a hidden crew is perfectly safe. 1 = as if they could see you.
Suspicion speed for 10 s after honking near them. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.

Suspicion speed in a vehicle of a side they are at war with (only when 'Own-side vehicles give cover'). 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.\nExample: 3 = a BLUFOR Hunter at an OPFOR checkpoint is identified three times as fast.
Line of sight respects the vehicle itself: glass lets some sight through, doors and roof block it.\nOff = only terrain and buildings block sight, the vehicle is see-through.
Within this distance the AI sees you just as well as up close. Farther away it gets harder fast.\nHigher = suspicion builds from farther away.\nExample: 40 = full effect inside 40 m.
At this suspicion the group sees through your disguise and attacks.\nLower = cover breaks sooner. 100 = only at full suspicion.
Chance per civilian group that witnesses it.
Time to make the report. Cancelled if the informant dies.
How far away a civilian can witness from.
Civilians who see a soldier get into a vehicle or a hostile act may report it.
Suspicion after passing an inspection. Nearby friendly groups drop to it too.
After passing an inspection that group will not pursue you again for this long.
%1 is inspecting your vehicle. Stay put - driving off now means you are identified.
Suspicion speed while being inspected (on top of face-to-face). 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
A foot patrol starts its inspection when your vehicle stops within this distance.
How long the inspection lasts. Survive it without being identified and you are cleared.
How much faster suspicion builds inside face-to-face range. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.\nExample: 4 = a guard at your window is four times as effective.
Within this distance a soldier is looking straight into the vehicle (checkpoint, walking past).\nHigher = the face-to-face bonus starts farther away.
With LAMBS Danger loaded, its group AI is paused while a group pursues, so it does not break the chase.
With LAMBS loaded, pursuers that identify you hand over to LAMBS Rush (on foot) or Hunt (mounted).

Pursuing groups never go farther than the limits below from where they were (their post or patrol spot).\nAt the edge they stop, and give up and radio if you stay beyond it.\nEach group can have its own limit (AI Group Profile module / setGroupProfile).
How far a foot group may go from home while chasing, searching or inspecting.
Give up beyond the limit after (s)
You stay beyond their roam limit this long and they give up (and alert, see 'Alert when you get away').
How far a mounted group may go from home while following you.
Suspicion speed with a weapon light or laser on at night. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
Suspicion speed driving at night with headlights off. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
How many soldiers of each group (closest to the vehicle first) get a line-of-sight check.\nHigher = more accurate in big groups, costs more CPU.\nEvery member counts, not only the group leader.

Enemy AI farther away than this can never become suspicious of a vehicle.\nLower = drive past distant positions freely. Higher = long-range observers matter.\nExample: 800 = a sniper team 1 km away ignores you.
Suspicion is remembered this long after you get out, so getting out and back in does not reset it.
Close to a group, a vehicle in plain view whose crew is hidden (reversing up to a checkpoint,\nparking rear-on) still builds suspicion through the vehicle itself. Armored vehicles are exempt.
Only vehicles slower than this are checked for hidden-crew tricks. A car driving past\nwhose crew happens to be out of sight is not a trick.
Extra suspicion speed after the full ramp time of hidden-crew tricks. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
Keep reversing or parking rear-on this long and the extra penalty below is at its maximum.
Hidden-crew tricks are only judged within this distance of a soldier.
How well a guard at face-to-face range sees you even through a closed body (they can lean in).\n0 = a closed hull fully protects. 1 = always seen perfectly up close.
What happens when someone in the vehicle has no cover (an exempt player, AI of another side).
They do not affect the others.
Each of them makes suspicion build faster (see 'Mixed crew multiplier').
One uncovered occupant blows the cover of the whole vehicle.
Suspicion speed for each uncovered person in the vehicle (when 'Uncovered people' = Faster suspicion). 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
How well the AI sees into vehicles in full darkness (scaled smoothly by sun and moon light).\n0 = blind at night. 1 = night makes no difference.
Hint when an enemy group identifies you. Per player.
Hint when you gain or lose cover. Per player.
Hint while an enemy patrol is inspecting your vehicle. Per player.
Hints when a truce starts, ends, is about to run out or is broken. Per player.
Hint when an enemy group becomes suspicious of you. Per player.
Curators get messages for identifications, bulletins, pursuits and truce breaks. Per player.
Suspicion speed with NVGs on the head during the day. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
Same as Darkness, for AI wearing night vision goggles.
Suspicion speed driving off-road within 150 m of a group. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
Comma-separated vehicle classes treated as open vehicles. Child classes are included.\nExample: Quadbike_01_base_F,Motorcycle
What happens in vehicles where everyone can see you (quad bikes, motorbikes, open boats).
You get cover, but suspicion builds faster (see 'Open vehicle multiplier').
Riding an open vehicle never hides you.
Suspicion speed on quads, bikes and other open vehicles (when they give cover). 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
Extra suspicion speed for each separate time you drive past the same group (circling, drive-bys).\nExample: 0.25 = second pass x1.25, third x1.5 ...
You must be out of sight this long before the next sighting counts as a new pass.
The repeated pass bonus never goes above this multiplier.
How well a soldier notices you outside their field of view.\n0 = not at all. 1 = as well as looking straight at you.
A group that reads a reported plate goes COMBAT at once.
Soldiers must be this close (with line of sight) to read a plate.
A reported vehicle's number plate is reported too: any vehicle with that plate is identified as soon as\nthe plate is read, whatever its side.
Suspicious and searching groups go after the vehicle with real waypoints: foot patrols run at it,\nmounted patrols follow it, signal it to stop and inspect it. Their own route resumes afterwards.
Pursuers head for where the vehicle will be in this many seconds.
A pursuit is abandoned once the group is this far from where it started.
Most groups that pursue the same unit at once. Keeps the whole map from converging on you.
Only groups within this distance start a pursuit.
A pursuit that has not led to a stop is abandoned after this long.
Comma-separated backpack classes that make a radioman (child classes included).
Comma-separated unit classes that count as radiomen. Classes with 'radio' in the name always count.
Which soldiers can send a bulletin.
Also anyone carrying a radio item.
How much rain hides you. 0 = rain does nothing. 1 = heavy rain hides you completely.
The ramming vehicle is recognised on sight by that side (within 'Known vehicle range'), so swapping\ncrews does not save it.

Ramming or running over a soldier, or ramming their vehicle, gets everyone undercover in your vehicle\nidentified by that group at once. Off = the group only becomes SUSPICIOUS (see Ramming suspicion).
Driving into or over enemy soldiers alerts their group at once.
Minimum speed for contact to count as ramming.
Suspicion given to the rammed group (at least SUSPICIOUS).
The vehicle counts as rear-on when the soldier is within this angle of straight behind it.
Suspicion speed when stopped or crawling with the back towards them and the crew hidden. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
SUSPICIOUS or SEARCHING groups calm down (UNAWARE) once suspicion falls below this.
Suspicion added to the pursuers when you refuse to stop.
How much the AI know about you once identified (0-4, the engine's knowsAbout).\n4 = they know exactly where you are.
Suspicion speed when reversing near them with the crew hidden. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.\nHigher = reversing through a checkpoint is a dead giveaway.
Moving backwards faster than this counts as reversing.

Suspicion speed in a vehicle of the exact faction watching you (CSAT truck at a CSAT checkpoint). 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.\nLower = they expect their own vehicles and barely look twice.
An enemy AI sitting in the same vehicle identifies everyone in it at once.\nOff = they build suspicion like everyone else.
Suspicion speed for groups that are already SEARCHING for you. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
Suspicion speed for passengers. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.\nLower = passengers in the back are harder to make out.
Suspicion speed for the driver. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
Suspicion speed in seats where you hold your weapon out of the window. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
Turned out (head out of the hatch)
Suspicion speed when turned out. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.\nHigher = sticking your head out is a giveaway.
Suspicion speed for gunners and commanders inside. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
Share of a group's earlier (non-witness) knowledge of you that turns into starting suspicion when you get in.\n0 = a clean slate every time. 1 = what they knew carries over fully.
Time before the information arrives. Killing the whole group first stops it.
A group already SUSPICIOUS or SEARCHING identifies the unit when it hears about it.
Groups this close to an identifying group see the reaction and identify at once. 0 = off.
How much receiving groups learn about the position (0-4) on a full share.
What friendly groups around learn when a group identifies someone.
Every group finds out on its own.
They become SEARCHING with the shared suspicion.
They identify the unit at once.
The identifying group needs a soldier with a radio to share.
Friendly groups within this distance of any member of the identifying group get the information.
Starting suspicion for groups that start searching.
Creates map markers for detection zones (visible to everyone).
How much the AI's spotting skills change suspicion speed.\n0 = skill does not matter. 1 = a skilled spotter is up to twice as fast, a poor one much slower.
Suspicion speed while speeding near a group. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
Driving faster than this within 100 m of a group is suspicious.
How much faster suspicion builds when parked near a group for the full ramp time. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
How long you must stay parked near a group before the loitering penalty is at its maximum.\nLower = parking near the enemy becomes suspicious sooner.
Adds 'Check cover status' to the ACE self-interaction menu while in a vehicle. Per player.
Pursuing vehicles honk to make you stop.
Pursuing vehicles flash their headlights to make you stop.
Not stopping within this long after the signal counts as refusing: they radio an alert.
At this suspicion the group becomes SUSPICIOUS: it may go alert, watch you, and you get a warning hint.\nLower = they react to you earlier.
Starting suspicion after the first switch.
An identified unit that switches to another vehicle unseen is only suspected again, not identified.\nThe old vehicle stays known.
How long a group remembers earlier switches.
The group must not have seen you for this long (and must not see you now) when you switch.
Extra starting suspicion for every earlier switch. Once it reaches 'Identified at', switching no longer works.
Off = synced suspicion stops just below 'Identified at', the receivers still need their own look.
Time for the information to pass (radio, shouting). Killing the senders first stops it.

While suspicion builds, nearby friendly groups get the same level after the sync delay.\nExample: the guards at a checkpoint's exit are as wary as the ones who watched you arrive.\nChanging vehicle, uniform, vest, helmet or weapon in between shakes it off.
Share of the sender's suspicion the receivers take. 1 = the same level. 0.5 = half.
How often a group passes on rising suspicion. Lower = closer to real time, more network traffic.
Suspicion below this is not passed on.
The sending group needs a soldier with a radio.
Groups within this distance of any member of the sending group receive it. -1 = use 'Share radius'.
Synced suspicion only sticks while you still have the same vehicle and kit the sender saw.
Time without contact before the knowledge is aged.
Optionally ages what EVERY side knows about an identified unit after it breaks contact (setTargetAge).
Taking a vehicle last used by an AI group makes it known to that side if the owners are near or see it.
Owners within this distance always notice the theft.
How often each enemy group re-checks every undercover player.\nLower = reacts faster but costs more CPU. Higher = cheaper but jumpier.\nExample: 1 = once per second (recommended).
How long aiming at an AI soldier is tolerated.
Aiming at AI breaks the truce
Pointing a weapon at an AI soldier for the time below breaks the truce.
Besides the groups inside the zone, groups within this distance of the offender (or seeing them) react.
When one player breaks the truce (shooting, hurting or ramming AI, overstaying)...
The offender's whole player group loses it.
All players in that zone lose it.
Breaking the truce triggers a bulletin
Groups reacting to a broken truce roll for a radio bulletin (see 'Radio Bulletins').
AI groups standing in a safe zone are CARELESS and hold fire until the truce is broken.
After a break, the players who lost the truce cannot get it back for this long, even by leaving and re-entering.

Inside a Safe haven zone the AI do not attack players of the zone's sides, not even on foot or\nonce identified, as long as the players behave. Made for roleplay areas (Zeus playing the locals).\nOff = safe zones only stop suspicion from building.
The truce lasts this long after leaving the zone, so the AI do not open fire at the border.
You left the safe zone: truce over.
How long players may stay in a safe zone before the truce ends. 0 = no limit.\nEach zone can set its own value in the Zone module.
The AI will not attack you while you stay peaceful.
The AI will not attack you while you stay peaceful. You may stay %1 s.
Players get a warning this long before their allowed stay runs out.
Safe zone: leave within %1 s or the truce ends.
Suspicion speed wearing civilian clothes. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
Suspicion speed wearing a military uniform of a side they are at war with (your own fatigues). 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
Suspicion speed wearing a uniform of the watching side or its allies. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
Comma-separated vehicle classes that never disguise anyone.\nExample: B_MRAP_01_F (the Hunter is too obviously NATO).
Comma-separated class:multiplier pairs that replace the faction multipliers. First match wins, child classes included.\nExample: O_MRAP_02_F:0.4,B_MRAP_01_F:5
Range multiplier for AI driving a vehicle (hatch closed). 1 = like the naked eye.\nLower = a driver behind a vision block sees less.

AI in a vehicle's gunner or commander seat (hatch closed) look through sights: they judge you\nfrom farther away. Only the range changes, not how wide they look.\nTurned out or firing-from-vehicle seats use their own eyes and weapons.

Range multiplier for AI behind vehicle optics. 1 = like the naked eye.
Higher = they read you from farther (and suspicion builds faster at a distance). Lower = worse than the naked eye.
Example: 1.5 = a BMP gunner 300 m away judges you as if you were 200 m away.
Each vehicle can set its own value (Vehicle Disguise module / setVehicleMode).
Comma-separated vehicle classes that always disguise, whatever their side.\nExample: C_Van_01_transport_F
If enemy AI shoot a covered vehicle anyway (it looked dangerous), they identify its occupants.
Suspicion speed wearing an armored vest. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
How long the wanted status lasts.
Suspicion speed against wanted units. 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
Suspicion speed when a rifle or launcher can be seen (turned out, firing seat, open vehicle). 1.0 = no change, 2.0 = twice as fast, 0.5 = half as fast.
A group that knows you this well (0-4, the engine's knowsAbout) and saw you just before you got in\nkeeps full knowledge: getting into a car in front of them does not fool them.
A group that saw you within this many seconds before you got in counts as a witness.
